arxiv-1901-07880.title: Phonetic-enriched Text Representation for Chinese Sentiment Analysis with Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-1901-07880.creator: Haiyun Peng, Yukun Ma, Soujanya Poria, Yang Li, Erik Cambria
arxiv-1901-07880.description: Abstract The Chinese pronunciation system offers two characteristics that distinguish it from other languages: deep phonemic orthography and intonation variations. We are the first to argue that these two important properties can play a major role in Chinese sentiment analysis. Particularly, we propose two effective features to encode phonetic information.

arxiv-2101-00682.description: Abstract . We prove a division algorithm for group rings of high genus surface groups and use it to show that some 2 2 -complexes with surface fundamental groups are standard. I would also like to thank the referees for their thorough reading. Thank you
arxiv-2209-00469.creator: Qing Liu
arxiv-2209-00469.description: Abstract . We describe an algorithm for determining a minimal Weierstrass equation for hyperelliptic curves over principal ideal domains. When the curve has a rational Weierstrass point w 0 w_{0} , we also give a similar algorithm for determining the minimal Weierstrass equation with respect to w 0 w_{0} .

arxiv-2209-08717.title: Dissipative magnetic structures and scales in small-scale dynamos 2022 Dissipative magnetic structures and scales in small-scale dynamos – B
arxiv-2209-08717.creator: Axel Brandenburg, Igor Rogachevskii, Jennifer Schober
arxiv-2209-08717.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Axel Brandenburg, Igor Rogachevskii, Jennifer Schober. Small-scale dynamos play important roles in modern astrophysics, especially on Galactic and extragalactic scales. Owing to dynamo action, purely hydrodynamic Kolmogorov turbulence hardly exists and is often replaced by hydromagnetic turbulence. Understanding the size of dissipative magnetic structures is important in estimating the time scale of Galactic scintillation and other observational and theoretical aspects of interstellar and intergalactic small-scale dynamos.

arxiv-2408-02442.title: Let Me Speak Freely? A Study on the Impact of Format Restrictions on Performance of Large Language Models
arxiv-2408-02442.creator: Zhi Rui Tam, Cheng-Kuang Wu, Yi-Lin Tsai, Chieh-Yen Lin, Hung-yi Lee, Yun-Nung Chen
arxiv-2408-02442.description: Abstract Structured generation, the process of producing content in standardized formats like JSON and XML, is widely utilized in real-world applications to extract key output information from large language models (LLMs). This study investigates whether such constraints on generation space impact LLMs’ abilities, including reasoning and domain knowledge comprehension.

arxiv-2503-12540.title: The topological spectrum of high dimensional quantum states
arxiv-2503-12540.creator: Robert de Mello Koch, Pedro Ornelas, Neelan Gounden, Bo-Qiang Lu, Isaac Nape, Andrew Forbes
arxiv-2503-12540.description: Abstract Topology has emerged as a fundamental property of many systems, manifesting in cosmology, condensed matter, high-energy physics and waves. Despite the rich textures, the topology has largely been limited to low dimensional systems that can be characterised by a single topological number, e.g., a Chern number in matter or a Skyrme number in waves.

arxiv-2504-09554.title: Mixture-of-RAG: Integrating Text and Tables with Large Language Models
arxiv-2504-09554.creator: Chi Zhang, Qiyang Chen, Mengqi Zhang
arxiv-2504-09554.description: Abstract . Large language models (LLMs) achieve optimal utility when their responses are grounded in external knowledge sources. However, real-world documents, such as annual reports, scientific papers, and clinical guidelines, frequently combine extensive narrative content with complex, hierarchically structured tables.

arxiv-2511-20931.creator: Biagio La Rosa, Leilani H. Gilpin
arxiv-2511-20931.description: Abstract Neurons are the fundamental building blocks of deep neural networks, and their interconnections allow AI to achieve unprecedented results. Motivated by the goal of understanding how neurons encode information, compositional explanations leverage logical relationships between concepts to express the spatial alignment between neuron activations and human knowledge.

pmc-10521345.creator: Agata Idziak, V. V. G. Krishna Inavalli, Stéphane Bancelin, Misa Arizono, U. Valentin Nägerl
pmc-10521345.description: Chemical fixation using paraformaldehyde (PFA) is a standard step for preserving cells and tissues for subsequent microscopic analyses such as immunofluorescence or electron microscopy (EM). However, chemical fixation may introduce physical alterations in the spatial arrangement of cellular proteins, organelles, and membranes.

pmc-10638438.creator: Svenja Palm, Bettina K. Doering, Thomas Kubiak, Katharina Geschke, Andreas Fellgiebel, Alexandra Wuttke
pmc-10638438.description: This study aimed to examine the influence of COVID-specific stressors on cross-sectional and longitudinal bereavement outcomes. According to the Dual Process Model of grief these stress-inducing factors can relate to the loss (loss-oriented stressors) or to manage everyday life (restoration-oriented stressors) and require coping in the grief process. A total of 491 participants (94.1% female; 43.92 years on average; 44.

pmc-11463745.title: New enantiornithine diversity in the Hell Creek Formation and the functional morphology of the avisaurid tarsometatarsus
pmc-11463745.creator: Alexander D. Clark, Jessie Atterholt, John B. Scannella, Nathan Carroll, Jingmai K. O’Connor, Felipe Lima Pinheiro, Felipe Lima Pinheiro, Felipe Lima Pinheiro, Felipe Lima Pinheiro
pmc-11463745.description: Enantiornithines were the most diverse group of birds during the Cretaceous, comprising over half of all known species from this period. The fossil record and subsequently our knowledge of this clade is heavily skewed by the wealth of material from Lower Cretaceous deposits in China.

pmc-11464663.title: Adaptive optics scanning laser ophthalmoscopy in a heterogenous cohort with Stargardt disease
pmc-11464663.creator: Mital Shah, Susan M Downes, Hannah E Smithson, Laura K Young
pmc-11464663.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Image based cell-specific biomarkers will play an important role in monitoring treatment outcomes of novel therapies in patients with Stargardt (STGD1) disease and may provide information on the exact mechanism of retinal degeneration. This study reports retinal image features from conventional clinical imaging and from corresponding high-resolution imaging with a confocal adaptive optics scanning laser ophthalmoscope (AOSLO) in a heterogenous cohort of patients with Stargardt (STGD1) disease.

pmc-11504392.title: Building an Ethical and Trustworthy Biomedical AI Ecosystem for the Translational and Clinical Integration of Foundation Models
pmc-11504392.creator: Baradwaj Simha Sankar, Destiny Gilliland, Jack Rincon, Henning Hermjakob, Yu Yan, Irsyad Adam, Gwyneth Lemaster, Dean Wang, Karol Watson, Alex Bui, Wei Wang, Peipei Ping, Kwang Woo Ahn
pmc-11504392.description: Foundation Models (FMs) are gaining increasing attention in the biomedical artificial intelligence (AI) ecosystem due to their ability to represent and contextualize multimodal biomedical data. These capabilities make FMs a valuable tool for a variety of tasks, including biomedical reasoning, hypothesis generation, and interpreting complex imaging data.

pmc-13372807.title: Quantifying the added value of foot-controlled force variables in predicting mild cognitive impairment
pmc-13372807.creator: Daniel Koska, Andresa Germano, Daniel Schmidt, Ann-Kathrin Harsch, Christian Maiwald
pmc-13372807.description: Predicting early cognitive decline is important for timely interventions. However, existing approaches for early detection remain limited by cost, scalability, or concerns about their validity. This study evaluated the potential of lower-extremity force control capacities, a largely unexplored area, to improve prediction of cognitive status in older adults with and without Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI).

pmc-13494327.title: A new sweetpotato variety ‘Michishizuku’ for alcohol and starch production with high yield and resistance to foot rot
pmc-13494327.creator: Akira Kobayashi, Yukari Kawata, Takeo Sakaigaichi, Keisuke Suematsu, Yumi Kai, Tetsufumi Sakai, Yasuhiro Takahata
pmc-13494327.description: We developed a new sweetpotato variety, ‘Michishizuku’, as the raw material for imo-shochu, a traditional Japanese distilled liquor made from sweetpotaoes, and for starch production. Michishizuku was selected from a cross between ‘Konaishin’ and Kyukei 09187-14 and was released in 2021.

pmc-13580112.title: PockLigGPT: Pocket-Sequence-Conditioned Molecular Generation with GPTs and RL
pmc-13580112.creator: Pablo Varas Pardo, Guillermo Marcos-Ayuso, Eugenia Ulzurrun, David Ríos Insua, Nuria E. Campillo
pmc-13580112.description: De novo drug design aims to generate molecules targeting specific protein pockets while retaining chemical plausibility and drug-like properties. Recent 3D structure-based generative methods explicitly model pocket-ligand geometry, but this does not always translate into chemically realistic or practically usable candidate molecules. Molecular language models provide a complementary sequence-based alternative.

pmc-13624461.title: Perceived Stress, TikTok Addiction, Self-esteem, and academic performance among university students in Saudi Arabia: A structural path analysis
pmc-13624461.creator: Manal Almalki
pmc-13624461.description: Background & Objectives:TikTok is widely used among university students in Saudi Arabia, raising concerns about its potential role as a maladaptive coping strategy. Limited research has examined how perceived stress, TikTok addiction, and self-esteem jointly influence academic performance within the General Strain Theory (GST) framework.
